spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, B are collinear with C between A and B; points A, D, B are collinear with D between A and B (both BC and BD are annexes to AB)
Rational line EF is set out; rectangle EG equal to sq(AB) applied to EF with breadth EH; rectangle HI equal to 2*rect(AC,CB) applied to EF with breadth HK
Rectangle EI (= EG + HI) equals sq(AC) + sq(CB), an additive arrangement of rectangles along EF
Rectangle EL equal to sq(AB) applied to EF with breadth EM; rectangle MI equal to 2*rect(AD,DB) applied to EF with breadth MN

configuration_map: The proof operates in two one-dimensional spaces: (1) a line containing collinear points A, D, B, C where AB is the second apotome of a medial and BC, BD are candidate annexes; (2) a rational line EF on which various areas (squares and doubled rectangles) are applied as rectangles, producing breadths that are then analyzed for commensurability. There are no two-dimensional geometric constructions, no triangles, no circles, no angles, no interior/exterior claims. Every operation is either a collinear point arrangement or the standard Book 10 technique of applying areas to a rational line to deduce commensurability properties of their breadths.
skip_reason: This is a purely algebraic/proportional proof in Book 10 commensurability theory. The proof deals entirely with medial lines, rational lines, commensurability/incommensurability relations, and the technique of applying areas to a rational line. There are no geometric configuration claims (no triangles, circles, angle decompositions, ray orderings, or interior/exterior arguments) that could harbor spatial contradictions. The only spatial content is trivial collinear point arrangements and standard area applications.
